newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA - LITIMPEKS BANK'S 1Q LOSSES 1.9 MLN LITAS.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA - LITIMPEKS BANK'S 1Q LOSSES 1.9 MLN LITAS.

text.p: Lithuania's Litimpeks Bank said on Thursday that its losses for the first three months of this year amounted to 1.9 million litas compared to a profit of 479,000 litas for the same period in 1996.
The bank's losses for 1996 were 6.37 million litas.
The bank's deputy chairman Edmundas Kachkus also told Reuters that the bank's assets fell slightly in the first three months of the year to 160.7 million litas from 163.6 million litas.
He said that the bank's net loan portfolio rose in the same period to 54.4 million litas from 49.2 million litas.
Its deposits in the first quarter of 1997 also increased, rising to 147.4 million litas from 144.6 million litas.
The bank last month decided to devalue its share capital from 40.9 million litas to 4.09 million litas and to launch a new 60 million litas share issue.
"We are intensively exchanging information about the bank with potential investors and partners," Kachkus said, adding that the bank was confident that the share issue would be a success.
He declined to name any potential investors.
Dealers say that Poland's Polska Kasa Opeky is the leading contender for investing into Litimpeks, which has had a troubled history.
The bank was shut late in 1995 after it was declared insolvent by the central bank.
It clawed its way back to solvency and the moratorium on its activities was lifted by the central bank last June.
